headline: Berg Lake Trail Permits and Highway Access
reservation: Overnight stays on the Berg Lake Trail require a highly competitive permit booked via the BC Parks reservation system, often months in advance. Day use of the lower trails currently does not require a permit, but rules are subject to annual review. Check the official portal for the latest status of trail reconstructions following glacial flood events.

days.title: The Base of the Emperor
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Kinney Lake
stops.detail: Hike the first section of the Berg Lake Trail to see the turquoise waters at the base of Mount Robson.

stops.name: Overlander Falls
stops.detail: Visit this powerful waterfall on the Fraser River, accessible via a short trail near the park entrance.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; easy access from Highway 16.
days.note: The trail to Kinney Lake is relatively flat and shared with cyclists on certain sections.

days.title: Alpine Meadows and High Passes
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Mount Fitzwilliam Trailhead

stops.name: Mount Fitzwilliam Trail
stops.detail: Ascend through subalpine forest toward rock gardens that provide views of the Robson Valley's southern end.

stops.name: Lucerne Lake
stops.detail: Stop at this lakeside area near the Alberta border for a picnic with views of the Continental Divide.

days.driving: Allow 30–40 minutes; watch for wildlife on the Yellowhead Highway.
days.note: This area is less crowded than the main Berg Lake corridor but requires more self-sufficiency.

days.title: Fraser River Headwaters
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from Tête Jaune Cache

stops.name: Rearguard Falls
stops.detail: Watch the Fraser River drop over a rocky ledge; this is the furthest point upstream for Chinook salmon migration.

stops.name: Jackman Flats Provincial Park
stops.detail: Explore the nearby sand dunes and unique lichen forest just outside the main Mount Robson gates.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; sites are located along a short stretch of the highway.
days.note: Rearguard Falls is a quick stop; Jackman Flats is better for a leisurely afternoon walk.

intel.title: Berg Lake Trail Status
intel.text: Significant portions of the upper Berg Lake Trail may be closed for repair due to environmental damage. Always verify the current 'open' distance at the Visitor Centre before starting your hike.

intel.title: Visitor Centre Congestion
intel.text: The main parking area is a popular stop for Highway 16 travelers. For the Berg Lake Trailhead, use the dedicated hiker lot further down the access road.

intel.title: Regional Services
intel.text: The closest reliable fuel and full-service groceries are in Valemount, BC, or Jasper, AB. A small seasonal store operates near the park entrance but has limited stock.

intel.title: Highway Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is generally available along Highway 16 but drops off immediately upon entering any side valleys or trails. Do not rely on data for backcountry navigation.

intel.title: Mount Robson Visibility
intel.text: The peak is famously shrouded in clouds; clear views are most common in the early morning. Plan your photography for the first light to maximize your chances.

plan.arrival: Arrive from Prince George (YXS) or Jasper; check in at the Visitor Centre to confirm trail conditions before heading to your campsite or lodge.
plan.vehicle: The region is well-suited for RVs with wide highway pullouts, but check length restrictions for some secondary parking lots.
plan.goldenHour: The viewpoint at the Mount Robson Visitor Centre provides a classic sunset vista of the South Face, though cloud cover is a frequent variable.
